summary: A 100-foot Tennessee Division of Forestry steel tower in Wayne County, photographed in 1942 and still used as a radio site; its build date and current condition are unknown.

access.note: Bottom flights of stairs removed to prevent climbing; Do Not Trespass signs noted in a March 2006 visit report; no newer access source found

events.note: Photograph dated 1942 in the register shows the tower already existed
Visit report by Jerry Lutes: bottom stairs removed, Do Not Trespass signs, not staffed
Registered January 3, 2015; nominated by Jerry Lutes

evidence.supports: located in Wayne County, west of Columbia and just off State Route 13
evidence.quote: located in Wayne County, west of Columbia and just State Route 13
It is a 100’ structure with diagonal stairs

evidence.supports: steel tower with diagonal stairs, 100 feet (visit report)
photograph dated 1942 shows the tower existed by then
evidence.quote: 1942 photo courtesy of Tennessee Secretary of State

evidence.supports: bottom flights of stairs removed to prevent climbing
evidence.quote: Bottom 1 and 1/2 flights of stairs removed to prevent climbing.

evidence.supports: Do Not Trespass signs on site

still used by the Division as a radio repeater site
evidence.quote: still used by the Tennessee Division of Forestry as a radio repeater site

evidence.supports: records of 1930s tower construction are scarce
evidence.quote: Due to the scarcity of surviving records associated with the construction of TDF’s fire lookout towers, the exact quantity and location of the fire towers constructed in the 1930s is unknown.

evidence.supports: many TDF towers erected in the 1930s with CCC partnership
evidence.quote: many of TDF’s fire lookout towers were erected in the 1930s in partnership with President Franklin D. Roosevelt Administration’s New Deal agency, the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC)

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, 1933 to 1975 (National Register multiple property documentation form)

notes_for_editor: No construction date found; the register gives no build year and the 1942 photograph is the earliest dated evidence. Access and staffing come from a March 2006 visit report, nearly 20 years old; 'closed' is an inference from the removed stairs and posted signs and should be checked. Do not merge with the Central US Lookouts 'Flatwoods' page: a search snippet describes a different CCC tower near Greenville Camp on Highway 67, which is not this one. The OSM record (lattice tower, 291 m) is not used.
